title: AI失控？：不是自主意识，是任务设定，谁在设定？
speaker: Robert Lee

segments.en: This is something that's afflicting both the Chinese and the AI developers, I suppose. When you talked to us also about humor here, when it comes to the risks on the security trends for the US model developers, I mean, we've seen that cyber feelings from OpenAI from Enthelpe, is that something that is also, you know, maybe when you look at the Chinese developers, they have a bit of a better hold on the security aspect of things.
segments.zh: 这困扰着中美AI开发者。谈到安全风险，我们看到OpenAI等公司的网络事件，但中国开发者可能在安全方面做得更好。

segments.en: It's a bit difficult to say enough, I'd say the Chinese market for maybe obvious reasons is better regulated or more regulated, it's just the nature of the beast and that's common with many end markets in China.
segments.zh: 很难说，但中国市场可能出于明显原因监管更严格，这是常态，在中国许多终端市场都是如此。

segments.en: And I will have to come back and answer this question maybe more fully another time. But again, with all these headlines at the moment about AI models going rogue and this to any other, my understanding is that many of them were set that task in the first place.
segments.zh: 我以后会详细回答。但关于AI模型失控的新闻，我的理解是很多模型最初就是被设定去执行那些任务的。

segments.en: So it wasn't as if they were sentient, they did this independently and off they went and started. But they were actually tasked with finding vulnerabilities and they're very, very good at that.
segments.zh: 并不是它们有意识，独立行动。实际上它们是被赋予寻找漏洞的任务，而且它们非常擅长。

segments.en: But that goes back to a central point I've continually made for, again, best part of three years. It's based on patent recognition, this is what these models are really, really good at.
segments.zh: 这又回到我三年来一直强调的核心观点：这些模型擅长模式识别。

segments.en: So yeah, they are good at exploiting vulnerabilities when they're tasked to do that but did they decide that autonomously, again are we going to see rising the machines, all these other scarce stories, I think it's a complete nonsense to be honest.
segments.zh: 它们在被要求时确实擅长利用漏洞，但它们是自主决定的吗？我们会不会看到机器崛起？我认为这些故事完全是胡说。
